source_row.extraction_instructions: Listing page /events/conferences renders ~70 upcoming events on one page as <li><div class="news-box"> cards; detail URLs are /events/conferences/detail/YYYY/MM/DD/default-calendar/<slug> and encode the event date in the URL path (use as a deterministic date fallback). Detail pages: key-info table (.table-block table tr, rows Location/CPD/Timings), pricing in .fees table tr (td=label, th=£price, sometimes multiple '/'-separated price+timeframe variants per cell), Overview/Programme prose inside .faq-accordion .panel-body. Skip any listing card whose <h3> title contains '[CANCELLED]'. IMPORTANT: this site's CloudFront edge 403s any request with 'HeadlessChrome' in the User-Agent, so both listing and detail fetches must go through httpx with a normal desktop Chrome UA string rather than a bare headless-Playwright navigation.

probe_results: Listing (httpx, desktop UA): 70 detail links found, matches page's own '70 Upcoming Events' heading; 1 filtered as [CANCELLED] -> 69 shells returned by list_shells_override(). Probed 3 different detail-page shapes plus 4 additional random samples (7 total): (1) multi-day priced conference with day-chip dates + member/grade fee table + conference-dinner add-on -> 11 tiers, correct Oxford venue/region, CPD=1, specialty 'Medical Psychotherapy'; (2) course page with fees TBC (no .fees block, no day chips, date only from URL) -> 0 tiers (correctly empty, not fabricated), Edinburgh venue, specialty 'Leadership & Management' via generic classifier, description correctly left null (no Overview panel exists, nav-junk excluded); (3) online single-fee workshop -> Location 'Online event' correctly mapped to event_format='online', venue/city null, 1 tier '£270'. 4 extra random samples all returned sane name/dates/venue/specialty/pricing-tier counts (0-8 tiers depending on source page).
notes: Key infra finding: rcpsych.ac.uk's CloudFront WAF blocks Playwright's default headless User-Agent (403 'The request could not be satisfied') on every navigate() call — confirmed via the shared BrowserController unmodified. Since browser.py cannot be edited, the extractor works around this entirely within rcpsych.py: list_shells_override() and extract_detail() both fetch HTML via httpx with a normal Chrome UA, then extract_detail() loads the fetched HTML into the (already-blocked) Playwright `page` via page.set_content() so all field extraction still uses page.evaluate()/DOM patterns consistent with other extractors (no bs4/lxml available in the venv, so this reuses the existing pattern rather than hand-rolled regex parsing). This same httpx-fetch approach is precedented in bopa.py, rcem.py, rcog.py etc. (already import httpx). Found and fixed two bugs during probing: (1) the page renders two <h1> tags (an empty one in site chrome + the real title) — querySelector('h1') alone silently returns empty; fixed by picking the first non-empty <h1>. (2) The shared specialty_classifier.py's generic 'General Practice' catch-all (matches on 'annual conference') mis-tags RCPsych faculty conference titles that don't literally contain 'psychiatr' (e.g. 'Faculty of Medical Psychotherapy Annual Conference') — added a small RCPsych-specific keyword pre-check (checked before the shared classifier, not editing the shared file) mapping faculty names (psychotherapy, neuropsychiatry, forensic, liaison, old age, etc.) to precise specialty labels, with 'Mental Health' as final default.
concerns: 1. This source's reliability now depends on rcpsych.ac.uk's CloudFront WAF continuing to allow requests with a normal desktop Chrome User-Agent from httpx — if their WAF starts fingerprinting httpx's TLS/HTTP2 signature too, this source would need a different bypass (e.g. a stealth-patched Playwright context), which would require touching shared browser.py and is out of scope here. 2. Course-type pages with fees/dates not yet published (layout #2) correctly return empty pricing_tiers/null start_date/null description — this is intentional 'come back next time' behaviour per PLAYBOOK, but means some RCPsych rows may sit with sparse data for a while until the college publishes fuller detail pages; the self-healing re-fetch logic in scraper.py (triggered by null event_format/venue/city) should pick these up, but won't retry purely for a null description on an in_person event with venue already known — acceptable per PLAYBOOK guidance. 3. The deterministic specialty heuristic occasionally over-fires on a loosely related keyword found deep in body text (e.g. one probed event titled 'Human Rights: Friend or Foe to Psychiatrist' got tagged 'Neuropsychiatry' rather than something more generic) — cosmetically imperfect but always within-domain (psychiatry-adjacent), and this only matters when the LLM call fails since LLM result wins when present. 4. default_event_type is 'mixed' per the task brief, but this extractor does not yet set event_type explicitly per-row (relies on title-heuristic + no course_sessions[] support) — RCPsych's 'Course' titles are still emitted as flat conference rows with a single date, not as course-type parent+sessions; flagging for a possible follow-up if RCPsych's occasional multi-run courses need the course_sessions[] treatment later.

source_row.extraction_instructions: This source publishes 14 fixed course types (APEx, APLS 2 Day, APLS Recertification, ATLS, CPRR, CYP APEx, HMIMMS, HMIMMS Team Provider, MIMMS 2 Day, MIMMS Team Provider, mMOET, NAPSTaR, PLS, POET) each on its own plain HTML page at /coursedates/courseview.php?coursetype=<TYPE> — no sitemap, no per-course subpage; the page itself is both listing and detail. Parse the single results <table> (header row: Start date/End date/Location/Centre-Venue/Apply Here/Telephone/Notes) into one course_sessions row per table row (dates DD-MM-YYYY), pulling venue/city from the Location + Centre/Venue columns and an optional GBP fee from free text in the Notes cell (most rows have none — leave price null rather than guess). There is no CPD info and no Overview/About prose anywhere on the site's public pages, so description/specialty must come from static per-course-type knowledge, not page scraping.

probe_results: Listing: list_shells_override() emits exactly 14 shells (one per hardcoded coursetype value, confirmed against the live <select id=\"coursetype\"> dropdown — no PHTLS, ATLS used instead, matches recon). Detail/session table probed across all 14 pages: 0 crashes, session counts ranged from 1 (APEx, CYP APEx, HMIMMS Team Provider, MIMMS Team Provider, POET) to 61 (APLS 2 Day) — total ~119 upcoming sessions site-wide. Pricing: only APLS 2 Day publishes inline GBP fees (7/61 rows have a £ figure in the Notes cell, e.g. £715.00, £490, £650); all other 13 course types currently show 0 sessions with a discoverable GBP price (organisers quote on contact) — correctly left empty, no fabrication. CPD: confirmed 0/14 pages mention CPD anywhere. Dates: DD-MM-YYYY parsed correctly on all 3 test pages; all sessions with unparseable/missing dates are dropped.
notes: Deviations from the standard playbook, both driven by real page structure (not laziness): (1) conference_name does NOT come from an h1 — the page's only h1 is the site logo/banner ("Course Dates and Venues"), identical on all 14 pages, so I use a static COURSE_TYPE_NAMES map keyed on the coursetype URL param instead, documented in the module docstring. (2) description/specialty have no page prose to summarize (no Overview/About section exists anywhere on the source), so I use a static, conservative COURSE_TYPE_DESC map rather than calling the LLM on near-empty content (playbook mistake #6/#9) — descriptions only claim facts I could verify from the page itself or extremely well-established course-name conventions (APLS/ATLS/MIMMS/HMIMMS names come straight from recon.json's expected_found list). For 5 acronyms I was NOT confident of the expansion (APEx, CPRR, NAPSTaR, POET — plus keeping mMOET's expansion moderate-confidence), I deliberately left the bare code rather than invent a wrong expansion. pricing_tables.py's shared table parser doesn't apply here — there's no labelled fee table, just free-text £ figures inside a Notes <td>, so I wrote a small inline regex parser (reusing BaseExtractor.parse_gbp) instead. Per the task's explicit filtering instruction, course_sessions only include upcoming (>= 2026-08-15) rows — this differs from the rcseng_courses.py reference pattern, which keeps all sessions and only filters for parent-field computation; I followed the task instruction over the reference file here.
concerns: 1. Availability status is 'unknown' for essentially every session (no explicit sold-out/limited markers observed anywhere across all 14 pages during probing) — this is correct per the playbook's guidance to prefer 'unknown' over guessing, but means the availability_status field will be low-signal for this source. 2. specialty_classifier is a shared file I could not edit; HMIMMS classified as \"Leadership & Management\" because its full name literally contains the word \"Management\" (Hospital Major Incident Medical Management and Support) — a benign but slightly misleading substring match inherent to the shared classifier, not something introduced by this extractor. Flagging rather than silently accepting in case a future session wants to add an \"Emergency Medicine\"/\"Major Incident Management\" rule ahead of the generic Leadership rule. 3. Venue/city are frequently None at the parent level (by design — most course types run at many different, unrelated regional providers so no single value is \"uniform\"); this is expected/correct behavior per the course-source model, not a bug. 4. I could not verify the acronym expansions for APEx, CPRR, NAPSTaR, POET, mMOET via any live ALSG page (main site is a login-gated Moodle VLE, WebFetch 500'd) — descriptions for those 4 stay generic/bare rather than risk a wrong claim; a future session with ALSG login access could tighten these.

source_row.extraction_instructions: Hub page /training-courses links ~22 bookable course pages (drop 'instructor-courses' category hub, 'information-instructors', and 'dentalprofessionals' — those are non-course info/hub pages with no h1 course template). Each course page server-renders a Drupal Views 'Course Availability' table listing dated upcoming sessions across independent Course Centres (town, centre name, start date, organiser contact, availability text), paginated via ?page=0..N at 5 rows/page; some courses (e.g. ILS, GIC) publish a centre directory with NO Start date column, or no table at all (e-learning/instructor courses) — in that case emit the course parent with zero sessions. Fees are NEVER published on-site (each Course Centre sets its own price locally and RCUK charges a flat per-candidate fee to the centre, not the learner) — do not fabricate pricing_tiers, always emit an empty list.

probe_results: list_shells_override() found 22 course shells from the hub (25 raw links minus 3 denylisted hub/info pages) via httpx, matching recon's ~25 estimate. extract_detail() tested on 3+ distinct shapes: (1) ALS 2-day — 5-column dated table, 74 sessions across 15 pages, includes a genuine sold_out row (verified 5/74 rows flagged sold_out correctly), CPD=10, format=in_person, end_date correctly +1 day from '2 Day Course' title match; (2) ILS — table present but only 3 columns (town/centre/organiser, no dates) → correctly yields 0 sessions, null dates/format (self-healing null, not fabricated); (3) NLS — 5-column dated table, 69 sessions, 1-day course, end_date==start_date; (4) GIC instructor course — no availability table at all (application-gated), 0 sessions, description pulled cleanly from body prose. Pricing always empty list across all pages, as required.
notes: A prior/parallel session had already written extractors/resus.py before I started; I read it against PLAYBOOK + fresh live probes rather than rewriting from scratch, found and fixed one real bug (HTML entities like '&' leaking into venue_name from the raw regex-parsed table cells — Warrington & Halton Teaching Hospitals Foundation Trust), added html.unescape() to the shared _strip_tags() helper inside resus.py, and re-verified all fixes against live pages. Listing/detail extraction uses httpx directly (server-rendered Drupal, js_required=false per recon.json) rather than Playwright DOM walks for both the hub and the paginated session tables — only the Playwright `page` object is used for h1/description/CPD-table/body-text reads on the already-loaded detail page, per PLAYBOOK mistake #10 (never navigate the page away mid-extraction).
concerns: specialty_classifier.py (shared, not editable per task rules) has no 'Emergency Medicine' / 'Resuscitation' / 'Critical Care' category at all, so the deterministic fallback misclassifies ALS/ILS/NLS/PILS courses as 'Paediatrics' (matched via generic 'young people'/'children' substrings elsewhere in body text) whenever the LLM call is unavailable. In production the LLM (llm_call) runs first and should classify these correctly as Emergency Medicine-adjacent; the deterministic backstop is just weak for this source. Not fixed since specialty_classifier.py is a shared file outside scope — flagging for a future classifier-rule addition rather than silently living with bad fallback data. Separately: 'anaphylaxis-essentials' is included as a course shell despite having no availability table (pure e-learning courses get a parent row with sessions=[] per RCSEng precedent) — this looked correct on inspection (legitimate RCUK-branded course), not a hub/info page, but worth a human glance the first time it lands in the DB.

source_row.source_name: Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow
source_row.extraction_instructions:
Detail pages at /education/ carry a

canonical name, an #education-date whose data-date attributes are already ISO (multiple

probe_results: Listing: browser.get_event_cards() mis-detects the community.rcpsg.ac.uk booking anchor as booking_url and the listing renders ONE CARD PER SESSION DATE (a course with N upcoming sessions produces N duplicate cards, all pointing to the same /education/<slug> detail page) -- so a list_shells_override() was required. It walks /education?sort=earliest&page=1..16 (stops after 2 consecutive empty pages; real content spans pages 1-11, ~10 cards/page, page 11 has 3, page 12+ empty) using a.hub-result-item-title anchors and dedupes by canonical path. Repeated live runs found 72-77 unique course/event detail URLs (page's own 'Showing 10 of 103' count reflects session-cards, not unique courses -- 103 minus dup cards matches the 72-77 unique range). Detail probes across 5 differently-shaped pages: (1) online course, 2 sessions -> 2 pricing tiers (Member £65/Non-member £105), event_type=course, event_format=online for both sessions; (2) single-date in-person conference (Glasgow Gastro) -> 5 pricing tiers via richer .tab-content[data-id^=fees] prose (Member/Non-member/AHP/Trainee/BSG), CPD=6, city=Glasgow/region=Scotland; (3) free multi-session workshop (Active Bystander Training, 7 sessions) -> 0 pricing tiers (correct -- genuinely free), CPD=4; (4) in-person course with 2 sessions (MRCS Part B) -> 2 tiers Member £499/Non-member £550; (5) single-date hybrid diploma (Travel Medicine, £4,545) -> after adding a label-stopword filter to reject prose false-positives ('The Diploma Fee Is £4,545', 'You Will Receive A £500' from payment-plan prose), correctly falls back to the clean .course-register-block summary for 2 tiers (Member/Non-member both £4,545).
notes: Session dates and locations come from data-date/data-location/data-url attributes on a #education-date <select><option> (2+ sessions) or a fallback <input> (exactly 1 session) -- dates are already ISO, no month-name parsing needed. Pricing has no HTML <table> markup on this source (all prose paragraphs), so extractors/pricing_tables.py's table parser does not apply; I wrote a bespoke regex ('Label: £X' pairs) with a word-count + stopword filter to reject prose false positives while keeping genuine short role-based tier labels (Member/Non-member/AHP/Trainee/BSG). Pricing is flat (session_id=None) for all probed courses -- no evidence any source page varies price by session date. City/region detection uses a small fixed lookup (Glasgow/Scotland plus a few other UK cities) since RCPSG venues are almost always its own building or Glasgow University's CASC -- never fabricates a city when the venue name doesn't contain a recognised city. list_shells_override() launches its own BrowserController instance (matching the RCSEngCourses precedent of a sitemap-based override) since browser.get_event_cards() cannot be reused here without either double-counting session-cards or capturing the wrong booking_url.
concerns: 1) The shared specialty_classifier.py produced a false positive ('Dentistry') on the Active Bystander Training page because the Overview text happens to mention 'dental professionals' among the healthcare roles it targets -- same class of bug already documented in the classifier's own docstring for RCSEng nav leakage. Per this repo's scope-fix convention (fix per-source, not the shared classifier, unless seen on >=2 sources) I left specialty_classifier.py untouched; in production the LLM call runs first and will very likely override this correctly, the heuristic is only the backstop. 2) Live listing counts varied slightly between two separate scrape runs (72 vs 77 unique URLs) because the Drupal pager's card set isn't perfectly stable page-to-page under sort=earliest -- harmless (dedup is by canonical path so nothing is double-inserted, and the daily cron will re-converge), but worth knowing the source doesn't guarantee a fully stable page->card mapping run-to-run. 3) No new-source scraper_sources row can be inserted by me (DB writes are out of scope for this task) -- the proposed row above needs to be inserted by the operator before source_id=25 will actually run.

source_row.source_name: Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh
source_row.extraction_instructions:
Listing is a server-rendered Foundation accordion (dd.accordion-navigation.courseItem) on services.rcsed.ac.uk, NOT WordPress/JS-rendered — walk ?page=1..5 (~15 items/page, ~75 total) reading the 'View more' anchor href as the detail URL. On the detail page, read the '.keyFacts' panel's 'When is this held?' / 'Where is this held?' / 'CPD' li items for dates/venue/CPD (panel is absent when no session is currently scheduled — leave dates null and retry next run). Fees appear under a 'Costs' or 'Course Fees' heading in one of two shapes:
  • Label: £X
    • or

    £X Label

    — parse both. If the 'When' text contains multiple date-groups separated by '/', treat it as a recurring course and emit one course_sessions row per group; otherwise it's a single-dated conference/workshop.

probe_results:
Listing: list_shells_override() (httpx, no browser) found all 75 shells across pages 1-5, matching the CMS's own 'Viewing X of 75' count and recon's volume_estimate=70. Detail probes across 6 different real pages: (1) advanced-trauma-life-support-atls — single date 25 Nov 2026, FULL/sold-out via badge span detection, Layout-B '

£X Label

' fees, 3 tiers, CPD 34h, venue=Edinburgh/RCSEd. (2) event-details-25th-qi-audit-symposium-2027 — date 'To be confirmed' (left null, correct self-healing behaviour), Layout-A '
  • Label: £X
    • ' fees (feesList), 3 tiers, CPD 6h. (3) basic-surgical-skills-cardiff — TWO date-groups '16th & 17th May / 11th & 12th July 2026' correctly split into 2 course_sessions with shared trailing year 2026, event_type='course', external venue Cardiff/Wales via UK region lookup, 1 flat price tier. (4) basic-microsurgical-skills-course-bms — single FULL date, confirms sold-out badge detection works independent of the ATLS case. (5) 10th-surgical-approaches-to-the-spine — no .keyFacts panel at all (self-paced/no scheduled instance): dates/venue/format correctly left null; also the page where I found and fixed a Cookiebot cookie-consent-banner contamination bug in the description LLM-fallback text. (6) 36th-advanced-otology-course — same no-keyFacts shape, confirms description/specialty fallback still produces clean text after the Cookiebot fix.
notes:
Two real bugs were found and fixed during probing (both would have shipped bad data if I'd stopped after 1-2 probes, exactly the PLAYBOOK warning about probing 3+ shapes): (1) the FULL/sold-out badge text runs directly into the next word with no space ('FULLJoin waiting list'), so a naive \\bFULL\\b regex silently failed — switched to detecting the '.label.alert' badge element itself. (2) pages with no literal 'Overview' heading (self-paced courses with no current session) were falling through to a raw document.body clone that included the Cybotebot cookie-consent dialog's full text ('This website uses cookies…') as the 'description' — fixed by (a) trying an H2/H3 that repeats the course title as a second-choice heading anchor, and (b) always stripping [class*=Cookiebot]/[class*=cookie] elements from the last-resort full-body fallback. Pricing has two coexisting HTML shapes on this source (feesList
  • vs bare

    £X Label

    ) — both handled, plus the shared pricing_tables.py table parser as a third-tier fallback per PLAYBOOK guidance (never triggered in my probes since RCSEd doesn't use for fees, but it's wired in). Course/session detection is heuristic: I split the 'When is this held?' text on '/' and treat 2+ resulting date-groups as a recurring course (event_type='course' + course_sessions[]), 1 group as a normal single-dated conference/workshop (event_type left unset, falls to the shared title-keyword heuristic in llm_agent.py). Session-level availability_status is intentionally left 'unknown' and booking_url=None — RCSEd's per-location booking dropdown text format (e.g. 'November 2026') was too coarse to reliably re-associate with a specific parsed multi-day session without risking a wrong match, and 'unknown' is an explicitly sanctioned value per the PLAYBOOK's course_sessions guidance rather than a guess.
concerns: 1. The date-group '/' split heuristic for detecting recurring courses vs single events is untested against the full 75-item catalogue — I only saw 2 concrete multi-date examples (basic-surgical-skills-cardiff). If RCSEd ever uses '/' for something other than a date separator (unlikely but unverified) it could misfire. 2. Session booking_url/availability_status are always null/'unknown' by design (see notes) — acceptable per PLAYBOOK but means course_sessions rows won't show live seat counts even when the source does display them, until a future refinement extracts the per-location dropdown more precisely. 3. Venue address is only fully populated for RCSEd's 3 known bricks-and-mortar sites (Edinburgh/Birmingham/Malaysia) plus a generic UK city/region lookup for external venues (e.g. Cardiff) — venue_name stays null for external venues since no structured address block was found on any probed page for those. 4. I did not run this against all 75 items or the full main.py pipeline (out of scope per task rules — no DB writes, no main.py) — only 6 detail pages + the full listing walk were verified live.

source_row.extraction_instructions:
Listing is one page with ~506 /event/.html cards grouped into
(upcoming) vs
(already happened) — only walk the non-'-past' divs to get upcoming events. Detail pages are server-rendered Preside CMS: title is the second

inside .banner-info-box (skip the cookie-banner and site-logo h1s), dates/CPD are in .banner-info-box p.date/p.credits, and fees live in a 'Registration Fees' tab as plain

Label: £X

lines (not an HTML table) rather than a sidebar price block. Venue is either a 'Location' tab with a free-text UK address, or plain online/Zoom text in the sidebar or the Book Now button's href domain (zoom.us/teams.microsoft.com) when no venue text exists at all.

probe_results: Listing: 78 upcoming shells found (matches recon's expected ~186 refs to 2026 + 18 to 2027 being an overcount of raw link mentions vs. unique dedicated events; the site's own events-YYYY vs events-YYYY-past div split cleanly separates 78 upcoming from 429 past across events-2025-past(260)+events-2026-past(169)). Category badges on cards: 'Webinar'->workshop (7 found), 'College conference'->conference (0 in current upcoming window), 'External Event' left unmapped (71) for title-heuristic fallback. Detail probes across 5 distinct shapes (external-hosted no fee/venue, tabbed single flat fee + online, tabbed free + in-person venue with address, tabbed two-tier free/paid + online, sidebar-only free + Zoom) all extracted h1/dates/CPD/pricing/venue/format correctly with deterministic fallbacks; description + specialty heuristic fallback (LLM stubbed to None in test) also populated on every page.
notes:
Used list_shells_override() with a plain httpx GET (Preside CMS is fully server-rendered, no JS needed, confirmed via direct httpx fetch containing tab content and £ prices with £ entities) rather than the shared browser DOM walker, because the walker has no way to express the site's own events-YYYY vs events-YYYY-past bucketing — that bucketing is the actual upcoming/past filter and is more reliable than parsing day-badges (which carry no month, only the enclosing year-block id). extract_detail() runs in the standard browser-navigated flow. Pricing uses a bespoke

Label: £X / - FREE

line parser (RCPath's fee tab is not an HTML , so pricing_tables.py's shared parser doesn't apply directly — it's still called as a supplementary fallback for any real-table cases, plus a Free-badge-driven £0 tier synthesis when no fee tab exists at all but the banner shows a 'Free' badge). Fixed one real bug during testing: the sidebar h3 lookup initially picked up unrelated 'More events'/'Featured' promo panel headings (e.g. 'World Patient Safety Day') as if they were venue names — fixed by restricting to h3 elements that are direct children of aside.sidebar (the real venue h3, e.g. 'Zoom', is a bare child; promo panels wrap their h3 in a nested .widget div).
concerns: 1. Deep RCPath specialty categories (Histopathology, Haematology, Microbiology, Cytopathology, Cellular Pathology etc.) are not in the shared specialty_classifier.py's keyword rules, so the heuristic fallback sometimes lands on generic/wrong buckets (observed 'Exam Preparation', 'GP Training', 'Leadership & Management', 'Paediatrics' on pathology-specific titles during LLM-stubbed testing) — in production the real LLM call will usually do better, and this is an existing shared-file limitation I was told not to edit, not a bug in this extractor. 2. Only 0 of the current 78 upcoming shells carry the 'College conference' badge (all currently-upcoming badged cards are 'Webinar' or unbadged 'External Event'), so the conference-type title-heuristic path for RCPath's own flagship conferences is untested against a live badged example this run — worth spot-checking after the first real scrape. 3. Venue address parsing (venue_name = text before the first city-name match) can look slightly odd on addresses where the city name appears twice (e.g. 'Belfast City Hospital' vs the trailing 'Belfast BT9 7AB') — it truncates at the first occurrence, which is imperfect but never fabricates data, consistent with the RCP reference extractor's same known limitation.
